subject: Recap + next steps: Aether pilot sizing, context mix & token economics
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena@aetheranalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + next steps: Aether pilot sizing, context mix & token economics

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have everything in one place. Please correct any assumptions.

Call highlights (what you told us)
- Primary use: meeting summarization + multi-document retrieval for customer-facing analytics reports. Mix of short transactional replies + long synthesized reports.
- Current throughput target: 10–20 daily active users for the first pilot; expected growth to ~200 DAUs in 6–9 months.
- Estimated monthly token volume (you mentioned rough ranges): 15M–40M tokens/month initially.
- Context needs: most flows require session context + 8k for recent conversation; ~20% of reports require 32k for multi-doc synthesis; occasional exploratory analytics could benefit from 128k but not required for pilot.
- Desired price target: you said ~ $300–$400 / 1M tokens to fit early-stage budget for hosted pilot.

Our initial unit-econ framing (back-of-envelope)
- Suggested pilot model choices: 32k window variant for synthesis flows (primary), 8k for transactional/faster paths.
- Avg prompt tokens (we estimate from your examples): 200–350 tokens.
- Avg completion tokens: 800–1,400 for the long-report paths; 40–200 for transactional replies.
- Expected token mix: ~60% prompts, 40% completions across workload but heavily skewed on completions for report generation.

Pricing scenarios (for conversation)
- Conservative: $420 / 1M tokens (no volume commitment) — gives us safety margin for heavy completions.
- Pilot-commit: $350 / 1M tokens with a 2-month pilot minimum of 20M tokens (or equivalent monthly usage over 2 months).
- Enterprise commit: $290 / 1M tokens at 100M+/month reserved capacity (discuss later).

Next steps I propose
1) We’ll send a short sizing worksheet for you to fill with an anonymized sample of 10 typical sessions (we attached a template).
2) We’ll prepare a formal pilot proposal (model selection, fallback policies, SLOs, and pricing table) by EOD Friday.
3) If procurement wants a PO path, loop in your procurement contact and we can produce an order + DocuSign link.

Attachments: pilot-plan-aether.pdf (pilot outline), aether-token-model-scenarios.xlsx (sizing worksheet).

If this looks right I’ll draft the pilot quote and loop in Aditya on the SOC2/audit evidence side.

Thanks — talk soon,
Karthik
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Aether pilot sizing, context mix & token economics

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirms everything from our side, with a couple clarifications:
- Our empiric averages from last month’s runs are a little different: avg prompt ~180 tokens; avg completion for the report pipeline ~1,200 tokens. Transactional flows are <100 completion tokens.
- The 15M–40M tokens estimate is on target if we include both prompts and completions.
- 32k window is a must for the multi-doc summarize use case; the 128k exploratory need is occasional and can be queued/batched initially.

Purchase path: please include a basic pilot SOW and estimated line items. Procurement (procure@aetheranalytics.com) wants a formal quote and a PO template — they’ll evaluate pricing against internal benchmarks. Also: SOC 2 Type II evidence and data retention policy (we need to review what’s stored, for how long).

I’ll fill the sizing sheet this week and return it. If you can get a draft quote on Friday that will help speed procurement.

—Lena
Head of Product
Aether Analytics

Karthik / Aditya —

Forwarding Lena’s confirmation. Quick internal notes / proposal to include in the Friday draft:

Sizing assumptions (fill in when we get their sheet)
- Pilot duration: 60 days.
- Pilot commit ask: 20M tokens over 60 days minimum to hit the Pilot-commit pricing tier.
- Model choices: start with 32k window for synthesis flows (default); 8k variant as lower-cost fallback for transactional flows.

Proposed pricing table (for inclusion in SOW)
- No-commit (pay-as-you-go): $420 / 1M tokens — general availability hosted price.
- Pilot-commit (20M over 60 days): $350 / 1M tokens (applies to all pilot usage, prorated).
- Optional: add a short-term burst credit to cap monthly overage at +20% over commit for the pilot.

Model routing & unit econ notes
- For synthesis jobs with avg 1,200 completion tokens and avg 300 prompt tokens, per-completion token cost dominates; show side-by-side $/1M for prompt vs completion if they request.
- Recommend enabling prefix KV cache for session-based flows to reduce repeated prompt tokens for long chat threads. Could reduce token volume 15–30% depending on UX.

Attachments to include in Friday deliverable
- Pilot plan PDF (attached)
- Token/model scenario XLSX (attached)

Aditya — can you pull SOC2 evidence links and a short summary of retention defaults we can share with procurement?

Marissa
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap + next steps: Aether pilot sizing, context mix & token economics

Nice summary, Marissa. A few decisions for the Friday draft:

1) Pilot configuration- Start with 32k model as default for synthesis (reporting) flows; route transactional/low-latency flows to 8k. Use 128k only for queued batch analytics (no real-time SLA).
2) Pilot pricing ask- Offer Lena the Pilot-commit at $350 / 1M tokens, conditioned on a 20M token minimum across the 60-day pilot OR a 10M/month soft target (we should pick the cleaner ask; I prefer the 20M/60d).
3) Acceptance criteria- SLO: 95th percentile latency < 900ms on 8k path; < 2.2s on 32k path for standard synth jobs. Quality: no more than 5% regressed summaries by their evaluation set (they’ll provide a sample).
4) SOC2 & procurement- Aditya please push SOC2 link and a one-page retention summary to include in the packet.

I’ll draft the quote lines showing three scenarios (no commit / pilot commit / enterprise) and include explicit $/1M rows for prompt tokens vs completion tokens for transparency.

Karthik
